section_1.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the two main branches of calculus through a physical scenario. Differentiation measures 'instantaneous change' (speedometer), while Integration measures 'total accumulation' (odometer). This section sets the stage for why we need to connect them.
section_1.example: An animated Cheetah accelerates across the screen. Above it, a graph shows its velocity. We pose the question: If we know the Cheetah's velocity at every second (Derivative), can we figure out the total distance it traveled (Integral) without adding up infinite tiny steps?

section_2.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
section_2.content: Briefly visualize the two operations independently. Differentiation as finding the slope of a tangent line; Integration as calculating the area under a curve using Riemann sums (thin rectangles).
section_2.example: A split-screen animation. On the left, a magnifying glass zooms into a curve to show a straight-line slope (dy/dx). On the right, a curve is filled with increasingly thin vertical bars to represent the area.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Area Function' A(x), which represents the area under a curve f(t) from a fixed point 'a' to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'bridge' concept. Explain that as 'x' moves, the area grows.
section_3.example: A 'Scanning Bar' moves from left to right across a graph of f(t). As it moves, the region behind it is shaded, and a new graph A(x) is plotted simultaneously above it, showing the total shaded area growing over time.

section_4.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 1. Show that the rate at which the area A(x) increases is exactly equal to the height of the function f(x) at that point. This proves that the derivative of an integral is the original function.
section_4.example: Zoom into the edge of the scanning bar. Show a tiny increase in width (dx). The tiny increase in area (dA) is a rectangle of height f(x) and width dx. Visually demonstrate dA/dx = f(x) using a 'puzzle piece' metaphor where the height of the curve determines the speed of area growth.

section_5.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
section_5.content: Explain the Evaluation Theorem. If Integration and Differentiation are inverses, we can calculate the area under f(x) simply by finding its antiderivative F(x) and calculating F(b) - F(a). No more infinite sums needed.
section_5.example: A 'Climb the Ladder' metaphor. To find the area under a velocity curve (f), we simply look at the height difference on the position ladder (F). The animation shows the area under a curve being 'poured' into a vertical cylinder to measure its height difference.

section_6.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
section_6.content: Conclude by emphasizing the perfect symmetry. Differentiation 'breaks down' a function into its rates; Integration 'builds up' those rates into a total value. They are two sides of the same coin.
section_6.example: A circular infographic showing a function f(x). An arrow pointing clockwise (differentiation) leads to f'(x), and an arrow pointing counter-clockwise (integration) leads back to f(x), forming a continuous loop of mathematical logic.

section_5.example: A 'Climb the Ladder' metaphor. To find the area under a velocity curve (f), we simply look at the height difference on the position ladder (F). The animation shows the area under a curve being 'poured' into a vertical cylinder to measure its height difference.

section_6.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
section_6.content: Conclude by emphasizing the perfect symmetry. Differentiation 'breaks down' a function into its rates; Integration 'builds up' those rates into a total value. They are two sides of the same coin.
section_6.example: A circular infographic showing a function f(x). An arrow pointing clockwise (differentiation) leads to f'(x), and an arrow pointing counter-clockwise (integration) leads back to f(x), forming a continuous loop of mathematical logic.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.
Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.
Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled.
animations: Cheetah silhouette (yellow: #FFFF00) moves from left to right across the screen.
Velocity graph (green: #00FF00) appears above the Cheetah, tracing its speed over time.
A speedometer icon (white: #FFFFFF) flashes to emphasize 'Differentiation' as instantaneous change.
An odometer icon (blue: #0000FF) appears, representing 'Integration' as total distance accumulated.
A question mark (white: #FFFFFF) appears between the speedometer and odometer icons.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
lecture_lines: Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.
Integrals calculate the area under a curve.
Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?
animations: A curve y = f(x) (red: #FF0000) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan (#00FFFF) Riemann rectangles.
The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
lecture_lines: Define the accumulation function as the area so far.
As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.
We denote this area function as A(x).
A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.
Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve.
animations: Function f(t) (yellow: #FFFF00) is plotted on a 2D plane with 'a' and 'x' marked on the axis.
A vertical scanning bar (white: #FFFFFF) starts at t = a and begins moving right.
The bar moves toward t = x, shading the area behind it in semi-transparent yellow (#FFFF00).
A new curve A(x) (blue: #0000FF) is drawn above the graph to track the total shaded area.
Labels 'f(t)' (yellow: #FFFF00) and 'A(x)' (blue: #0000FF) appear next to their respective curves.

section_4.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
lecture_lines: Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.
This narrow strip has a width of dx.
Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).
Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).
The derivative of the integral is the original function.
animations: Zoom into the right edge of the shaded area A(x) at the specific point x.
The boundary moves a tiny distance Δx (white: #FFFFFF), creating a thin vertical slice.
The slice is highlighted as a rectangle with height f(x) (green: #00FF00) and width dx.
The equation dA = f(x) * dx appears in white (#FFFFFF) next to the slice.
The derivative notation d/dx [A(x)] = f(x) appears and flashes in bright white (#FFFFFF).

section_5.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
lecture_lines: We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.
If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.
Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.
F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.
This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums.
animations: A curve f(x) (orange: #FFA500) is shown with the area between boundaries a and b shaded.
The antiderivative function F(x) (magenta: #FF00FF) is plotted on a separate scale above f(x).
Vertical markers at a and b show the height difference F(b) - F(a) on the F(x) curve.

section_6.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
lecture_lines: Calculus reveals a beautiful symmetry in change.
Differentiation and integration are perfect inverses.
Together, they bridge the gap between change and accumulation.
animations: The text 'f(x)' appears in the center of the screen in white (#FFFFFF).
A red (#FF0000) arrow circles 'f(x)' clockwise, labeled 'Differentiate' to show the forward path.
A blue (#0000FF) arrow circles 'f(x)' counter-clockwise, labeled 'Integrate' to show the reverse path.

outline.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
outline.content: Introduce the two main branches of calculus through a physical scenario. Differentiation measures 'instantaneous change' (speedometer), while Integration measures 'total accumulation' (odometer). This section sets the stage for why we need to connect them.
outline.example: An animated Cheetah accelerates across the screen. Above it, a graph shows its velocity. We pose the question: If we know the Cheetah's velocity at every second (Derivative), can we figure out the total distance it traveled (Integral) without adding up infinite tiny steps?

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Visual bridge effect: highlight the symmetry loop

            diff_label.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            int_label.animate.set_color("#0000FF"),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth", 
            [
                "Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.",
                "This narrow strip has a width of dx.",
                "Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).",
                "Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).",
                "The derivative of the integral is the original function."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#00FF00"  # Green for f(x)
        COLOR_DX = "#FFFFFF" # White for dx
        COLOR_DA = "#FFFFFF" # White for dA
        COLOR_RESULT = "#FFFFFF" # White for final derivative

        # Setup Axes
        # Belief B035: Expand grid by one row/column for Axes and use scale_factor 0.8-0.85
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": BLUE_D},
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E5", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        # Define function f(x) = 0.1*(x-1)**2 + 1.5
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * (x - 1)**2 + 1.5, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=BLUE_B)
        func_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE_B).scale(0.7)
        # Position label near end of curve
        self.place_at_grid(func_label, "B5")

        # Initial area A(x) up to x=2
        x_val = 2.0
        area_initial = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[0.5, x_val], color=BLUE_E, opacity=0.5)
        
        # Vertical bar at x
        scanning_bar = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val, func.underlying_function(x_val)),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        x_label = MathTex("x", color=WHITE).scale(0.7)
        # Position manually relative to axes since grid points might not align with 'x'
        x_label.move_to(axes.c2p(x_val, -0.3))

        self.add(axes, func, func_label, area_initial, scanning_bar, x_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DA)
        
        dx_val = 0.4
        area_increment = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[x_val, x_val + dx_val], color=YELLOW, opacity=0.7)
        
        # Highlight the area increment clearly.
        self.play(Create(area_increment), run_time=1.5)
        
        da_label = MathTex("dA", color=COLOR_DA).scale(0.7)
        # Position dA label relative to the slice
        da_label.move_to(axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val/2, func.underlying_function(x_val) + 0.5))
        
        self.play(Write(da_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This narrow strip has a width of dx.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_DX)
        
        dx_brace = BraceBetweenPoints(
            axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, 0),
            direction=DOWN,
            color=COLOR_DX,
            buff=0.1
        )
        dx_text = dx_brace.get_tex("dx", color=COLOR_DX).scale(0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(dx_brace), Write(dx_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_F)
        
        # Highlight height with a line
        height_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, func.underlying_function(x_val + dx_val)),
            color=COLOR_F,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        f_x_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.7)
        # Position label to the right of the height line
        f_x_label.next_to(height_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(height_line), Write(f_x_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_DA)
        
        # Equation dA = f(x) * dx
        eq_slice = MathTex(r"dA \approx f(x) \cdot dx", color=COLOR_DA).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_slice, "A4")
        
        self.play(Write(eq_slice))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The derivative of the integral is the original function.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_RESULT)
        
        # Final FTC equation
        ftc_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} [A(x)] = f(x)", color=COLOR_RESULT).scale(0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_eq, "F4")
        
        self.play(Write(ftc_eq))
        self.play(Indicate(ftc_eq, color=COLOR_RESULT, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.",
            "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.",
            "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        GRAPH_COLOR = "#00FF00"    # Green
        SPEED_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"    # White
        ODO_COLOR = "#0000FF"      # Blue
        QM_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"       # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette representation
        cheetah_body = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        cheetah_head = Circle(radius=0.12, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).move_to(cheetah_body.get_right() + UP*0.1)
        cheetah_leg1 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + LEFT*0.2)
        cheetah_leg2 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + RIGHT*0.2)
        cheetah = VGroup(cheetah_body, cheetah_head, cheetah_leg1, cheetah_leg2)
        
        # Velocity graph axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Parabolic-like velocity curve
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2 + 0.5 * x, x_range=[0, 5], color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        graph_label = MathTex("v(t)", color=GRAPH_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_label, 'A6')

        # Tracker for cheetah movement and graph tracing
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Movement bounds
        start_pos = self.grid['E1']
        end_pos = self.grid['E6']
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Use add_updater for movement
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 5)
        ))
        
        # Dot on graph tracing velocity
        dot = Dot(color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 0.1 * time_tracker.get_value()**2 + 0.5 * time_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(axes, graph_label)
        self.play(Create(graph), FadeIn(cheetah), run_time=2)
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SPEED_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer icon (White)
        speed_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE)
        speed_needle = Line(ORIGIN, 0.4 * UP + 0.1 * RIGHT, color=RED)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_arc, speed_needle)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.play(Flash(speedometer, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ODO_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer icon (Blue)
        odo_box = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.4, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odo_val = Text("123.4", font_size=16, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odometer = VGroup(odo_box, odo_val)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Question mark between icons
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=QM_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(question_mark, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(odometer))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(question_mark))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with the section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices",
            [
                "Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.",
                "Integrals calculate the area under a curve.",
                "Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?"
            ]
        )

        # Define colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FFFF"    # Cyan
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FFFF00"     # Yellow
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualization: A curve y = f(x) (red) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
        
        # Left-side of the grid for Differentiation (A1 to F3)
        axes_diff = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4],
            y_range=[0, 4],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_diff, "A1", "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5
        curve_diff = axes_diff.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Tangent line at x = 2
        point_x = 2
        dot = Dot(axes_diff.c2p(point_x, func(point_x)), color=WHITE)
        tangent_line = axes_diff.get_tangent_line_at_phi(point_x, curve_diff, length=2).set_color(COLOR_TANGENT)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        self.play(
            Create(axes_diff),
            Create(curve_diff),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualization: Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan Riemann rectangles.
        
        # Right-side of the grid for Integration (A4 to F6)
        axes_int = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4],
            y_range=[0, 4],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=3,

    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "The Accumulation Function"
        lines = [
            "Define the accumulation function as the area so far.",
            "As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.",
            "We denote this area function as A(x).",
            "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.",
            "Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        YELLOW_C = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"
        BLUE_C = "#0000FF"

        # Math Functions
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.5 * np.sin(t) + 1.2

        def a_func(x):
            # Integral of f_func from 0 to x:
            # \int (0.5*sin(t) + 1.2) dt = -0.5*cos(t) + 1.2*t
            return -0.5 * np.cos(x) + 1.2 * x

        # 1. Setup Axes
        # Using [B035]: expand bounding grid (A1-F6) and scale 0.8
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5.5,
            y_length=5.5
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # 2. Objects for Animation
        # Using [B079]: raw strings for LaTeX
        f_graph = axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=YELLOW_C)
        f_label = MathTex(r"f(t)", color=YELLOW_C)
        # Using [B066]: Verify orientation (B6 is right-side)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Marks
        a_val = 0.5
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(a_val)
        
        a_line = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(a_val, f_func(a_val)), color=WHITE_C)
        a_tex = MathTex("a", color=WHITE_C).next_to(axes.c2p(a_val, 0), DOWN)
        
        # Area and Scanning Bar

        shaded_area = always_redraw(lambda:

                x_range=[a_val, x_tracker.get_value()],
                color=YELLOW_C,
                opacity=0.3
            )

            MathTex("x", color=WHITE_C).next_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0), DOWN)
        )

        # Accumulation Graph
        # A(x) = \int_a^x f(t) dt
        a_graph = always_redraw(lambda:
            axes.plot(
                lambda t: a_func(t) - a_func(a_val),
                x_range=[a_val, max(a_val + 0.01, x_tracker.get_value())],
                color=BLUE_C
            )
        )
        a_label_tex = MathTex(r"A(x)", color=BLUE_C)
        self.place_at_grid(a_label_tex, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_C)
        self.play(Create(f_graph), Write(f_label))

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.add(shaded_area, scanning_bar, x_tex)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "We denote this area function as A(x)."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(Write(a_label_tex), Create(a_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE_C)

import numpy as np

        def get_rects():
            return axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(

            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,

        )

            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(rects),
            FadeIn(final_area),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map the right side of the screen (x from 0.5 to 5.5)
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0
                # Map the vertical space (y from 2.2 to -2.8)
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus", [
            "Calculus reveals a beautiful symmetry in change.",
            "Differentiation and integration are perfect inverses.",
            "Together, they bridge the gap between change and accumulation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The text 'f(x)' appears in the center of the right-side layout.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to prevent LaTeX compilation errors (Belief B008)
        fx = Text("f(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        # Position f(x) in the top-center area of the right-side layout
        self.place_in_area(fx, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(fx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight transition to second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # f'(x) appears at the bottom to form a symmetry loop
        f_prime = Text("f'(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(f_prime, "E3", "E4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Red clockwise arrow (Right side of the loop) representing Differentiation
        # Starting slightly right of fx and ending slightly right of f_prime
        diff_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E5"], angle=-TAU/4, color="#FF0000")
        diff_label = Text("Differentiate", font_size=18, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Blue counter-clockwise arrow (Left side of the loop) representing Integration
        # Starting slightly left of f_prime and ending slightly left of fx
        int_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["E2"], self.grid["B2"], angle=-TAU/4, color="#0000FF")
        int_label = Text("Integrate", font_size=18, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(int_label, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Animate the second half, completing the circle

            Create(int_arrow),
            Write(int_label)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to the summary line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Visual bridge effect: highlight the symmetry loop to emphasize unity
        self.play(
            fx.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            f_prime.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            diff_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            int_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            fx.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            f_prime.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            diff_label.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            int_label.animate.set_color("#0000FF"),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the two main branches of calculus through a physical scenario. Differentiation measures 'instantaneous change' (speedometer), while Integration measures 'total accumulation' (odometer). This section sets the stage for why we need to connect them.
section_1.example: An animated Cheetah accelerates across the screen. Above it, a graph shows its velocity. We pose the question: If we know the Cheetah's velocity at every second (Derivative), can we figure out the total distance it traveled (Integral) without adding up infinite tiny steps?

section_2.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
section_2.content: Briefly visualize the two operations independently. Differentiation as finding the slope of a tangent line; Integration as calculating the area under a curve using Riemann sums (thin rectangles).
section_2.example: A split-screen animation. On the left, a magnifying glass zooms into a curve to show a straight-line slope (dy/dx). On the right, a curve is filled with increasingly thin vertical bars to represent the area.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Area Function' A(x), which represents the area under a curve f(t) from a fixed point 'a' to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'bridge' concept. Explain that as 'x' moves, the area grows.
section_3.example: A 'Scanning Bar' moves from left to right across a graph of f(t). As it moves, the region behind it is shaded, and a new graph A(x) is plotted simultaneously above it, showing the total shaded area growing over time.

section_4.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
section_4.content: Demonstrate the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 1. Show that the rate at which the area A(x) increases is exactly equal to the height of the function f(x) at that point. This proves that the derivative of an integral is the original function.
section_4.example: Zoom into the edge of the scanning bar. Show a tiny increase in width (dx). The tiny increase in area (dA) is a rectangle of height f(x) and width dx. Visually demonstrate dA/dx = f(x) using a 'puzzle piece' metaphor where the height of the curve determines the speed of area growth.

section_5.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
section_5.content: Explain the Evaluation Theorem. If Integration and Differentiation are inverses, we can calculate the area under f(x) simply by finding its antiderivative F(x) and calculating F(b) - F(a). No more infinite sums needed.
section_5.example: A 'Climb the Ladder' metaphor. To find the area under a velocity curve (f), we simply look at the height difference on the position ladder (F). The animation shows the area under a curve being 'poured' into a vertical cylinder to measure its height difference.

section_6.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
section_6.content: Conclude by emphasizing the perfect symmetry. Differentiation 'breaks down' a function into its rates; Integration 'builds up' those rates into a total value. They are two sides of the same coin.
section_6.example: A circular infographic showing a function f(x). An arrow pointing clockwise (differentiation) leads to f'(x), and an arrow pointing counter-clockwise (integration) leads back to f(x), forming a continuous loop of mathematical logic.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.
Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.
Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled.
animations: Cheetah silhouette [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] (yellow: #FFFF00) moves from left to right across the screen.
Velocity graph (green: #00FF00) appears above the Cheetah, tracing its speed over time.
A speedometer icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg] (white: #FFFFFF) flashes to emphasize 'Differentiation' as instantaneous change.
An odometer icon (blue: #0000FF) appears, representing 'Integration' as total distance accumulated.
A question mark (white: #FFFFFF) appears between the speedometer and odometer icons.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
lecture_lines: Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.
Integrals calculate the area under a curve.
Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?
animations: A curve y = f(x) (red: #FF0000) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan (#00FFFF) Riemann rectangles.
The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.

section_3.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
lecture_lines: Define the accumulation function as the area so far.
As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.
We denote this area function as A(x).
A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.
Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve.
animations: Function f(t) (yellow: #FFFF00) is plotted on a 2D plane with 'a' and 'x' marked on the axis.
A vertical scanning bar (white: #FFFFFF) starts at t = a and begins moving right.
The bar moves toward t = x, shading the area behind it in semi-transparent yellow (#FFFF00).
A new curve A(x) (blue: #0000FF) is drawn above the graph to track the total shaded area.
Labels 'f(t)' (yellow: #FFFF00) and 'A(x)' (blue: #0000FF) appear next to their respective curves.

section_4.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
lecture_lines: Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.
This narrow strip has a width of dx.
Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).
Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).
The derivative of the integral is the original function.
animations: Zoom into the right edge of the shaded area A(x) at the specific point x.
The boundary moves a tiny distance Δx (white: #FFFFFF), creating a thin vertical slice.
The slice is highlighted as a rectangle with height f(x) (green: #00FF00) and width dx.
The equation dA = f(x) * dx appears in white (#FFFFFF) next to the slice.
The derivative notation d/dx [A(x)] = f(x) appears and flashes in bright white (#FFFFFF), accompanied by the based icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg].

section_5.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
lecture_lines: We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.
If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.
Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.
F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.
This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums.
animations: A curve f(x) (orange: #FFA500) is shown with the area between boundaries a and b shaded.
The antiderivative function F(x) (magenta: #FF00FF) is plotted on a separate scale above f(x).
Vertical markers at a and b show the height difference F(b) - F(a) on the F(x) curve.

section_6.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
lecture_lines: Calculus reveals a beautiful symmetry in change.
Differentiation and integration are perfect inverses.
Together, they bridge the gap between change and accumulation.
animations: The text 'f(x)' appears in the center of the screen in white (#FFFFFF).
A red (#FF0000) arrow circles 'f(x)' clockwise, labeled 'Differentiate' to show the forward path.
A blue (#0000FF) arrow circles 'f(x)' counter-clockwise, labeled 'Integrate' to show the reverse path.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.",
            "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.",
            "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        GRAPH_COLOR = "#00FF00"    # Green
        SPEED_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"    # White
        ODO_COLOR = "#0000FF"      # Blue
        QM_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"       # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette representation
        cheetah_body = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        cheetah_head = Circle(radius=0.12, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).move_to(cheetah_body.get_right() + UP*0.1)
        cheetah_leg1 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + LEFT*0.2)
        cheetah_leg2 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + RIGHT*0.2)
        cheetah = VGroup(cheetah_body, cheetah_head, cheetah_leg1, cheetah_leg2)
        
        # Velocity graph axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Parabolic-like velocity curve
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2 + 0.5 * x, x_range=[0, 5], color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        graph_label = MathTex("v(t)", color=GRAPH_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_label, 'A6')

        # Tracker for cheetah movement and graph tracing
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Movement bounds
        start_pos = self.grid['E1']
        end_pos = self.grid['E6']
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Use add_updater for movement
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 5)
        ))
        
        # Dot on graph tracing velocity
        dot = Dot(color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 0.1 * time_tracker.get_value()**2 + 0.5 * time_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(axes, graph_label)
        self.play(Create(graph), FadeIn(cheetah), run_time=2)
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SPEED_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer icon (White)
        speed_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE)
        speed_needle = Line(ORIGIN, 0.4 * UP + 0.1 * RIGHT, color=RED)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_arc, speed_needle)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.play(Flash(speedometer, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ODO_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer icon (Blue)
        odo_box = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.4, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odo_val = Text("123.4", font_size=16, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odometer = VGroup(odo_box, odo_val)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Question mark between icons
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=QM_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(question_mark, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(odometer))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(question_mark))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with the section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices",
            [
                "Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.",
                "Integrals calculate the area under a curve.",
                "Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?"
            ]
        )

        # Define colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FFFF"    # Cyan
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FFFF00"     # Yellow
        
        # Function to use for both visuals
        def func(x):
            return 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualization: A curve y = f(x) (red) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
        
        # Left half of the animation area
        axes_diff = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=2.5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_diff, "A1", "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve_diff = axes_diff.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Tangent line at x = 2.0
        point_x = 2.0
        # For a curve plotted from x=0 to 3.5, alpha for x=2.0 is 2.0/3.5
        alpha_val = point_x / 3.5
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve_diff, alpha=alpha_val, length=2.5, color=COLOR_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes_diff.c2p(point_x, func(point_x)), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_diff),
            Create(curve_diff),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualization: Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan Riemann rectangles.
        
        # Right half of the animation area
        axes_int = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=2.5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_int, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve_int = axes_int.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Initial coarse Riemann rectangles
        rects = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.5,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        # Highlight lecture line 2
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_int),
            Create(curve_int),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(rects),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualization: The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.
        
        # Highlight lecture line 3
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Refined rectangles (Step 1: Increase count)
        rects_fine = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.08,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0.2
        )
        
        # Final solid area
        final_area = axes_int.get_area(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            opacity=0.8
        )
        
        # Animate the transition from coarse rectangles to fine to solid area
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, rects_fine),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, final_area),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "The Accumulation Function"
        lines = [
            "Define the accumulation function as the area so far.",
            "As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.",
            "We denote this area function as A(x).",
            "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.",
            "Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        YELLOW_C = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"
        BLUE_C = "#0000FF"

        # Math Functions
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.5 * np.sin(t) + 1.2

        def a_func(x):
            # Integral of f_func from 0 to x:
            # \int (0.5*sin(t) + 1.2) dt = -0.5*cos(t) + 1.2*t
            return -0.5 * np.cos(x) + 1.2 * x

        # 1. Setup Axes
        # Using [B035]: expand bounding grid (A1-F6) and scale 0.8
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5.5,
            y_length=5.5
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # 2. Objects for Animation
        # Using [B079]: raw strings for LaTeX
        f_graph = axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=YELLOW_C)
        f_label = MathTex(r"f(t)", color=YELLOW_C)
        # Using [B066]: Verify orientation (B6 is right-side)
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Marks
        a_val = 0.5
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(a_val)
        
        a_line = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(a_val, f_func(a_val)), color=WHITE_C)
        a_tex = MathTex("a", color=WHITE_C).next_to(axes.c2p(a_val, 0), DOWN)
        
        # Area and Scanning Bar
        # [B010]: Use persistent objects for animation
        shaded_area = always_redraw(lambda:
            axes.get_area(
                f_graph,
                x_range=[a_val, x_tracker.get_value()],
                color=YELLOW_C,
                opacity=0.3
            )
        )
        
        scanning_bar = always_redraw(lambda:
            Line(
                axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
                axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), f_func(x_tracker.get_value())),
                color=WHITE_C,
                stroke_width=4
            )
        )

        x_tex = always_redraw(lambda:
            MathTex("x", color=WHITE_C).next_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0), DOWN)
        )

        # Accumulation Graph
        # A(x) = \int_a^x f(t) dt
        a_graph = always_redraw(lambda:
            axes.plot(
                lambda t: a_func(t) - a_func(a_val),
                x_range=[a_val, max(a_val + 0.01, x_tracker.get_value())],
                color=BLUE_C
            )
        )
        a_label_tex = MathTex(r"A(x)", color=BLUE_C)
        self.place_at_grid(a_label_tex, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Define the accumulation function as the area so far."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_C)
        self.play(Create(f_graph), Write(f_label))
        self.play(Create(a_line), Write(a_tex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.add(shaded_area, scanning_bar, x_tex)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "We denote this area function as A(x)."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(Write(a_label_tex), Create(a_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=3)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Topic: The Bridge Between Change and Accumulation
        # Section 5: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut
        
        self.setup_layout("FTC Part 2: The Shortcut", [
            "We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.",
            "If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.",
            "Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.",
            "F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.",
            "This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        COLOR_f = "#FFA500"  # Orange
        COLOR_MATH = YELLOW

        # Function definitions
        f_func = lambda x: 0.5 * x + 1.0
        F_func = lambda x: 0.25 * x**2 + x + 0.5
        a_val, b_val = 1.0, 4.0

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        axes_f = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=2.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_f, "D2", "F6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        curve_f = axes_f.plot(f_func, color=COLOR_f)
        label_f = MathTex(r"f(x)", color=COLOR_f).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_f, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        area_f = axes_f.get_area(curve_f, x_range=[a_val, b_val], color=COLOR_f, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_f), Create(curve_f), Write(label_f))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_f))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        axes_F = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 12, 2],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=2.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_F, "A2", "C6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        curve_F = axes_F.plot(F_func, color=COLOR_F)
        label_F = MathTex(r"F(x)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_F, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_F), Create(curve_F), Write(label_F))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        p_a = axes_F.c2p(a_val, F_func(a_val))
        p_b = axes_F.c2p(b_val, F_func(b_val))
        
        dot_a = Dot(p_a, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        dot_b = Dot(p_b, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        line_a = axes_F.get_vertical_line(p_a, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        line_b = axes_F.get_vertical_line(p_b, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        
        # Correct horizontal line generation
        h_line_a = axes_F.get_horizontal_line(p_a, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        h_line_b = axes_F.get_horizontal_line(p_b, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        
        label_Fa = MathTex(r"F(a)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.6)
        label_Fb = MathTex(r"F(b)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.6)
        
        label_Fa.next_to(axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(a_val)), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_Fb.next_to(axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(b_val)), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(line_a), Create(line_b), Create(h_line_a), Create(h_line_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(dot_b), Write(label_Fa), Write(label_Fb))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        y_start = axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(a_val))
        y_end = axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(b_val))
        
        brace_F = BraceBetweenPoints(y_start, y_end, direction=LEFT, color=COLOR_MATH, buff=0.5)
        brace_text = MathTex(r"F(b)-F(a)", color=COLOR_MATH).scale(0.6).next_to(brace_F, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(brace_F), Write(brace_text))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(area_f, color=COLOR_MATH),
            Indicate(brace_text, color=COLOR_MATH),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        sum_formula = MathTex(r"\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*) \Delta x", color=GRAY).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_formula, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        cross = Cross(sum_formula, color=RED)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_formula))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus", [
            "Calculus reveals a beautiful symmetry in change.",
            "Differentiation and integration are perfect inverses.",
            "Together, they bridge the gap between change and accumulation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The text 'f(x)' appears in the center of the right-side layout.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to prevent LaTeX compilation errors (Belief B008)
        fx = Text("f(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        # Position f(x) in the top-center area of the right-side layout
        self.place_in_area(fx, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(fx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight transition to second line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # f'(x) appears at the bottom to form a symmetry loop
        f_prime = Text("f'(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(f_prime, "E3", "E4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Red clockwise arrow (Right side of the loop) representing Differentiation
        # Starting slightly right of fx and ending slightly right of f_prime
        diff_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E5"], angle=-TAU/4, color="#FF0000")
        diff_label = Text("Differentiate", font_size=18, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Blue counter-clockwise arrow (Left side of the loop) representing Integration
        # Starting slightly left of f_prime and ending slightly left of fx
        int_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["E2"], self.grid["B2"], angle=-TAU/4, color="#0000FF")
        int_label = Text("Integrate", font_size=18, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(int_label, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Animate the first half of the logic bridge
        self.play(
            Create(diff_arrow),
            Write(diff_label),
            Write(f_prime)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate the second half, completing the circle
        self.play(
            Create(int_arrow),
            Write(int_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to the summary line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Visual bridge effect: highlight the symmetry loop to emphasize unity
        self.play(
            fx.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            f_prime.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            diff_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            int_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            fx.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            f_prime.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            diff_label.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            int_label.animate.set_color("#0000FF"),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
outline.content: Explain the Evaluation Theorem. If Integration and Differentiation are inverses, we can calculate the area under f(x) simply by finding its antiderivative F(x) and calculating F(b) - F(a). No more infinite sums needed.
outline.example: A 'Climb the Ladder' metaphor. To find the area under a velocity curve (f), we simply look at the height difference on the position ladder (F). The animation shows the area under a curve being 'poured' into a vertical cylinder to measure its height difference.

storyboard.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
lecture_lines: We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.
If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.
Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.
F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.
This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums.
animations: A curve f(x) (orange: #FFA500) is shown with the area between boundaries a and b shaded.
The antiderivative function F(x) (magenta: #FF00FF) is plotted on a separate scale above f(x).
Vertical markers at a and b show the height difference F(b) - F(a) on the F(x) curve.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Topic: The Bridge Between Change and Accumulation
        # Section 5: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut
        
        self.setup_layout("FTC Part 2: The Shortcut", [
            "We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.",
            "If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.",
            "Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.",
            "F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.",
            "This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta
        COLOR_f = "#FFA500"  # Orange
        COLOR_MATH = YELLOW

        # Function definitions
        f_func = lambda x: 0.5 * x + 1.0
        F_func = lambda x: 0.25 * x**2 + x + 0.5
        a_val, b_val = 1.0, 4.0

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        axes_f = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=2.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_f, "D2", "F6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        curve_f = axes_f.plot(f_func, color=COLOR_f)
        label_f = MathTex(r"f(x)", color=COLOR_f).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_f, "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        area_f = axes_f.get_area(curve_f, x_range=[a_val, b_val], color=COLOR_f, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_f), Create(curve_f), Write(label_f))
        self.play(FadeIn(area_f))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        axes_F = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 12, 2],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=2.0,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 20}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_F, "A2", "C6", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        curve_F = axes_F.plot(F_func, color=COLOR_F)
        label_F = MathTex(r"F(x)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(label_F, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_F), Create(curve_F), Write(label_F))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        p_a = axes_F.c2p(a_val, F_func(a_val))
        p_b = axes_F.c2p(b_val, F_func(b_val))
        
        dot_a = Dot(p_a, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        dot_b = Dot(p_b, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        line_a = axes_F.get_vertical_line(p_a, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        line_b = axes_F.get_vertical_line(p_b, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        
        # Correct horizontal line generation
        h_line_a = axes_F.get_horizontal_line(p_a, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        h_line_b = axes_F.get_horizontal_line(p_b, color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        
        label_Fa = MathTex(r"F(a)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.6)
        label_Fb = MathTex(r"F(b)", color=COLOR_F).scale(0.6)
        
        label_Fa.next_to(axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(a_val)), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_Fb.next_to(axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(b_val)), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(line_a), Create(line_b), Create(h_line_a), Create(h_line_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(dot_b), Write(label_Fa), Write(label_Fb))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        y_start = axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(a_val))
        y_end = axes_F.c2p(0, F_func(b_val))
        
        brace_F = BraceBetweenPoints(y_start, y_end, direction=LEFT, color=COLOR_MATH, buff=0.5)
        brace_text = MathTex(r"F(b)-F(a)", color=COLOR_MATH).scale(0.6).next_to(brace_F, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\int_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(brace_F), Write(brace_text))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_MATH)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(area_f, color=COLOR_MATH),
            Indicate(brace_text, color=COLOR_MATH),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        sum_formula = MathTex(r"\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i^*) \Delta x", color=GRAY).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_formula, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        cross = Cross(sum_formula, color=RED)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sum_formula))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with the section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices",
            [
                "Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.",
                "Integrals calculate the area under a curve.",
                "Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?"
            ]
        )

        # Define colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FFFF"    # Cyan
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FFFF00"     # Yellow
        
        # Function to use for both visuals
        def func(x):
            return 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualization: A curve y = f(x) (red) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
        
        # Left half of the animation area
        axes_diff = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=2.5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_diff, "A1", "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve_diff = axes_diff.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Tangent line at x = 2.0
        point_x = 2.0
        # For a curve plotted from x=0 to 3.5, alpha for x=2.0 is 2.0/3.5
        alpha_val = point_x / 3.5
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve_diff, alpha=alpha_val, length=2.5, color=COLOR_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes_diff.c2p(point_x, func(point_x)), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_diff),
            Create(curve_diff),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualization: Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan Riemann rectangles.
        
        # Right half of the animation area
        axes_int = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=2.5,
            y_length=2.5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_int, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve_int = axes_int.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Initial coarse Riemann rectangles
        rects = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.5,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        # Highlight lecture line 2
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_int),
            Create(curve_int),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(rects),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualization: The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.
        
        # Highlight lecture line 3
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Refined rectangles (Step 1: Increase count)
        rects_fine = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.08,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0.2
        )
        
        # Final solid area
        final_area = axes_int.get_area(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            opacity=0.8
        )
        
        # Animate the transition from coarse rectangles to fine to solid area
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, rects_fine),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, final_area),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.example: An animated Cheetah accelerates across the screen. Above it, a graph shows its velocity. We pose the question: If we know the Cheetah's velocity at every second (Derivative), can we figure out the total distance it traveled (Integral) without adding up infinite tiny steps?

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.",
            "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.",
            "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        GRAPH_COLOR = "#00FF00"    # Green
        SPEED_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"    # White
        ODO_COLOR = "#0000FF"      # Blue
        QM_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"       # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette representation
        cheetah_body = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=0.3, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        cheetah_head = Circle(radius=0.12, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).move_to(cheetah_body.get_right() + UP*0.1)
        cheetah_leg1 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + LEFT*0.2)
        cheetah_leg2 = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.25, color=CHEETAH_COLOR, stroke_width=4).move_to(cheetah_body.get_bottom() + RIGHT*0.2)
        cheetah = VGroup(cheetah_body, cheetah_head, cheetah_leg1, cheetah_leg2)
        
        # Velocity graph axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Parabolic-like velocity curve
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2 + 0.5 * x, x_range=[0, 5], color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        graph_label = MathTex("v(t)", color=GRAPH_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_label, 'A6')

        # Tracker for cheetah movement and graph tracing
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Movement bounds
        start_pos = self.grid['E1']
        end_pos = self.grid['E6']
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Use add_updater for movement
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 5)
        ))
        
        # Dot on graph tracing velocity
        dot = Dot(color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 0.1 * time_tracker.get_value()**2 + 0.5 * time_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(axes, graph_label)
        self.play(Create(graph), FadeIn(cheetah), run_time=2)
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SPEED_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer icon (White)
        speed_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color=WHITE)
        speed_needle = Line(ORIGIN, 0.4 * UP + 0.1 * RIGHT, color=RED)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_arc, speed_needle)
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.play(Flash(speedometer, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ODO_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer icon (Blue)
        odo_box = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.4, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odo_val = Text("123.4", font_size=16, color=ODO_COLOR)
        odometer = VGroup(odo_box, odo_val)
        self.place_at_grid(odometer, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Question mark between icons
        question_mark = Text("?", font_size=48, color=QM_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(question_mark, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(odometer))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Write(question_mark))
        self.wait(3)
